az_white_wall_the_2.blurb: A basalt crag in the Paradise Forks cluster of Sycamore Canyon, roughly half an hour west of Flagstaff near Williams. This is a trad wall with about two dozen lines, and the grades skew hard: most fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, a couple reach 5.13, and easier options are scarce, so it suits strong crack climbers rather than beginners. The columnar rock is hard and takes secure gear, and climbers usually reach the cliff from above, fixing a rope and rappelling in. Routes at the Forks are short, about 90 feet at most.

az_hidden_world_south.blurb: A small bouldering area in the Oak Flat zone of Queen Creek Canyon, about an hour east of Phoenix off US 60 near Superior. The problems sit on north-facing volcanic tuff walls, which makes the spot a sensible pick on warmer days. Nearly all of the 22 problems are easy, most around V0 with a few reaching V3, so it works well for beginners or for racking up a big session of moderates. You get there by following a trail of large cairns across a wash and up a slab.

az_ufo_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of desert boulders in the Icecapades zone on the north edge of Phoenix, off the end of Stetson Valley Parkway. Twenty-two problems cover the whole range, from a few beginner lines to a couple of very hard ones at the top end, with about half falling between V3 and V5. The boulders are rounded, the landings are decent, and the cove sits mostly in shade. The walk is short but crosses a bridge and a low wall, then follows a web of desert trails, so carry a map or GPS track. Access around here has shifted as housing has gone up nearby, so confirm the current situation before you drive out.

az_south_face_3.blurb: The main multi-pitch face of Rappel Rock, near the top of Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, at roughly 8,000 feet. Its 22 trad routes include some of the longest moderate lines on the mountain, many running 400 to 500 feet. Most climbs sit between 5.7 and 5.9, with a few harder lines at 5.10 and 5.11 and above. Temperatures are cool and the views reach south toward Tucson. The trail down and around the east side is steep and vague, so expect some route-finding. Raptors nest here, and the face may be off-limits from about February through July; if birds are active, climbers are asked to go elsewhere.

az_welcome_boulder_aka_triangle_boulder.blurb: A free-standing limestone boulder at Priest Draw, south of Flagstaff, and the first thing visitors meet on arrival. It is known for steep to vertical warm-ups and a good selection of elimination lines, and a small wall behind it adds more problems. Of the 22 problems, most run from V0 to V5, with a handful of very hard ones in the double digits, so it suits mixed groups. Priest Draw is workable through much of the year, and most of the draw gets sun. It is a quick walk from the signed parking area, and the community looks after the draw, so pack out what you bring.

az_main_wall_11.blurb: The tallest wall in Higher Solitude, a dacite sport crag high on the west side of Mount Elden above Flagstaff. Its 22 bolted routes run from 5.10 up to 5.13, split fairly evenly across the four grade bands, and most are about 70 to 100 feet of long, exposed, colorfully streaked rock. The stone is sharp and can be loose in places, so test your holds. It works well as a cold-weather crag, with winter sun reaching the face in the morning and shade arriving late in the afternoon during warm months. The hike is long and steep, and weekdays are usually quiet.

az_the_middle.blurb: A west-facing wall on Easter Peak in the Granite Dells outside Prescott, reached from the Peavine Trail. Its 22 trad lines run from easy fifth class to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.10 and many going two pitches. The upper part of the wall has very good rock, and cleaning has helped, but lines that see little traffic can still shed loose stone, so wear a helmet. Anchors along the ridge allow top-roping or rappelling off. The trail in is rough and finishes with a short scramble, so watch for people below you. The wall is shaded in the morning and sunny by early afternoon.
